title: Journal & analytics
body:
## Context
R3 "Trading on demo" (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 7) closes the execution loop: once orders are placed from the ticket, the chart and the DOM, fanned out across accounts and managed by rules, the owner needs evidence of what actually happened. **E41 Journal & analytics** is that evidence layer. The roadmap scopes it (section 7.2) as: *"Auto-captured trades from OMS executions with chart snapshots at entry/exit; manual notes, tags and rating; performance analytics (win rate, expectancy, R-multiple distribution, MAE/MFE, session/symbol/tag breakdowns, equity curve); per-account and per-trade-group views; CSV/Parquet export; `GET /v5/position/closed-pnl` reconciliation against local records"* - 26 pts, Sprints S18-S19, backend module **M20 `journal`**, story domain **JRN**.

Three properties make this more than a CRUD screen:
1. **The journal is derived, not authored.** Entries are materialised from the execution stream (M14 OMS) and must be idempotent and restart-safe (US-JRN-001 NFR). A user may only add *opinion* - notes, tags, rating, setup, mistakes; every computed field is read-only by contract (`updateJournalTrade` description in `22-api-openapi.yaml`).
2. **It is evidence, therefore tamper-evident and role-scoped.** `04-security-program.md` classifies journal content as asset **A-12**, requires exports to be role-scoped, watermarked and audited (**SR-098**), and rates journal export disclosure as threat **S4**. Journal write events (`journal.note_added`, `journal.tag_added`, `journal.tag_removed`, `journal.trade_excluded`, `journal.rating_set`) are audited, not merely analytics.
3. **Environments must never be mixed.** Live, demo/paper and replay-simulated results are separate populations (US-JRN-006 "Environment separation"; `journal_trades.env`, `journal_trades.is_paper`). Aggregating them produces a statistic worse than no statistic.

## Scope / Deliverables
**User stories (all 10 JRN stories):** US-JRN-001 (Must), US-JRN-002 (Must), US-JRN-003 (Should), US-JRN-004 (Should), US-JRN-005 (Should), US-JRN-006 (Must), US-JRN-007 (Should), US-JRN-008 (Should), US-JRN-009 (Should), US-JRN-010 (Could).

**Screens:** SCR-093 Journal (trade list, `/journal`), SCR-094 Trade detail / post-mortem, SCR-095 Journal analytics dashboard (`/journal/analytics`), SCR-096 Journal tag manager.

**Components:** CMP-166 JournalEntryRow, CMP-167 JournalEquityCurveChart, CMP-168 JournalStatsSummaryCard, CMP-169 TagEditor (new); reused CMP-021, CMP-024, CMP-026, CMP-036, CMP-043, CMP-044, CMP-046, CMP-047, CMP-049, CMP-055, CMP-058, CMP-099, CMP-116.

**API:** `GET /journal/trades`, `GET|PATCH /journal/trades/{journalTradeId}`, `GET|POST /journal/trades/{journalTradeId}/notes`, `GET /journal/trades/{journalTradeId}/context`, `GET|POST /journal/tags`, `GET /journal/analytics`; consumer of `GET /executions/closed-pnl`.

**DB:** `journal_trades`, `journal_tags`, `journal_trade_tags`, `notes` (plus `audit_log` writes and `executions` / `trade_groups` / `trade_group_legs` reads).

**Module:** M20 `journal` (`services/api/journal/`), with Parquet/DuckDB cold-tier reads for long-range analytics (C18).

## Out of scope
- Backtesting and strategy reports (R4/R5 epics) - the journal reports what happened, not hypotheticals.
- The replay engine itself (E26) - E41 only deep-links into it via `journal_trades.replay_anchor_ts`.
- Alert delivery channels (E40) - E41 only requests a notification when an async export finishes.
- Admin audit-log screens (E42); order/position management screens (E29/E30).
- Any Android client, any separate admin application, any non-Bybit / non-USDT-perp instrument.
- Broker statement import, tax reporting, third-party journal sync.

## Exit criteria
1. Every closed position on demo produces exactly one journal entry per account leg plus one `is_aggregate` row per trade group, correct after an API restart mid-close, verified against `GET /executions/closed-pnl`.
2. SCR-093/094/095/096 shipped, design-signed-off, axe-core clean, keyboard-complete, with table alternatives for every chart.
3. `GET /journal/analytics` returns totals and all seven breakdowns for 10 000 trades within budget (p95 <150 ms warm; breakdown query <=2 s cold), computed server-side.
4. Demo/live/paper populations are never aggregated together; the active environment filter is always displayed.
5. Export is role-scoped server-side, watermarked, audited, and contains no API identifiers or secrets.
6. STRIDE model (E41-X01) finalised and findings triaged; QA sign-off (E41-Q03) recorded.

## Story list
| Key | Title | Pts |
|---|---|---|
| E41-K01 | Spike: analytics query tier (Postgres vs DuckDB/Parquet) + ADR | 2 |
| E41-T01 | M20 journal module, migrations and read API | 3 |
| E41-T02 | Trade materialiser, MAE/MFE and closed-pnl reconciliation | 5 |
| E41-T03 | Analytics aggregation service and `GET /journal/analytics` | 3 |
| E41-T04 | Tags, notes, auto-tagging and audited export job | 3 |
| E41-T05 | Statistics formula reference + ADR-0016 | 1 |
| E41-S01 | Journal trade list screen (SCR-093) | 5 |
| E41-S02 | Trade detail / post-mortem (SCR-094) with replay deep-link | 3 |
| E41-S03 | Analytics dashboard (SCR-095) | 3 |
| E41-S04 | Tag manager (SCR-096) and export UI | 1 |
| E41-D01..D05 | UX research, wireframes, hi-fi, a11y review, handoff, design QA | 13 |
| E41-Q01..Q03 | Test plan + E2E, perf/chaos, a11y audit + regression + sign-off | 8 |
| E41-X01..X02 | STRIDE threat model + abuse cases, security review | 5 |

Engineering subtotal **29 pts** (roadmap budget 26, +11.5%, inside the +/-15% tolerance); design 13, QA 8, security 5 are tracked separately.

## Risks
- **R7 Data accuracy** - divergence between local P&L and `closed-pnl` silently misleads; mitigated by nightly reconciliation with a divergence alert (E41-T02).
- **R12 Backtest bias** - statistics on a <=20-trade sample look authoritative; mitigated by the mandatory low-sample caveat (US-JRN-006) and low-confidence bucket marking (US-JRN-008).
- **R13 Sharing abuse** - exports leak other managers' account data; mitigated by SR-098 server-side scoping, watermark and audit (E41-X01/X02).
- **R15 Data lifecycle** - snapshots and recorded context pruned before review; mitigated by an honest "context not recorded" state and the snapshot budget policy (US-JRN-004).
- **R5 Scope** - MAE/MFE and tag breakdowns are the declared R5 descoping candidates (`30-release-roadmap.md` section 12 row 7); they are built last and behind clear seams.


## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: End-to-end capture
  Given a fan-out trade group of three accounts opens and fully closes on demo
  When I open /journal
  Then three leg entries and one aggregate entry exist with weighted-average entry and exit prices
  And each entry's realised P&L matches GET /executions/closed-pnl within one quantisation step

Scenario: Environment separation
  Given both demo and live-flagged entries exist
  When I open /journal/analytics
  Then demo entries are excluded by default, the active environment filter is displayed, and no statistic mixes the two populations

Scenario: Scoped export
  Given I am an Account Manager with access to exactly one account
  When I export the journal
  Then the file contains only that account's trades, is watermarked with my identity and the timestamp, is audited, and contains no API key identifiers
```

## Technical notes / design
M20 owns a `TradeMaterialiser` subscribing to the OMS execution stream, a `JournalAnalyticsService` over the storage tier chosen by E41-K01, and the FastAPI router mounted at `/api/v1/journal`. Writes go to Postgres; long-range analytics may read Parquet via DuckDB (C18). All money maths crosses into `Decimal` at the module boundary per `24-internal-schemas.md` constraint C3.

## Test plan
Delegated to children and rolled up by E41-Q01 (functional/E2E), E41-Q02 (perf on 10k trades + chaos), E41-Q03 (a11y + regression + sign-off).

## Security notes
Asset A-12; threats S4 (export disclosure) and IDOR on `journalTradeId`; controls SR-098 plus deny-by-default `journal:read` / `journal:write` scoped to `granted_accounts`. Epic labelled `security`; STRIDE kickoff is E41-X01.

## Accessibility notes
Four screens, three of them data-dense. Every chart needs a table alternative and a text summary; colour is never the sole encoding (the MAE/MFE scatter encodes outcome by shape); signed values are always unit-labelled.

## Performance notes
SCR-093 virtualised to 10 000 rows at <=8 ms scripting per frame; SCR-095 interactive <=800 ms for 10 000 trades; breakdown queries <=2 s; REST reads p95 <150 ms (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 13).

## Observability
`journal_entries_materialised_total`, `journal_materialiser_lag_seconds`, `journal_reconciliation_divergence_total`, `journal_analytics_query_seconds`, `journal_export_rows_total`; audit events `journal.*` as enumerated on SCR-093/094/096.

## Definition of Done
Per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 2.2 - all children Done or explicitly descoped; epic-level AC verified end-to-end; coverage gates green; docs updated; WCAG 2.2 AA verified; STRIDE finalised and triaged; QA epic-level regression pass recorded; demoed to Owner; retro notes captured.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E29 (executions are the journal's only source of truth), E09 (RBAC scoping must exist before any account-scoped read), E34 (trade-group legs define the per-leg/aggregate shape). Soft consumers: E26 (replay deep-link), E40 (export-ready notification), E05 (design system).

title: UX research + wireframes for the journal surfaces (SCR-093..096)
body:
## Context
E41 introduces four brand-new surfaces (SCR-093 Journal list, SCR-094 Trade detail / post-mortem, SCR-095 Analytics dashboard, SCR-096 Tag manager) and a new interaction the product has not had before: **retrospective review** rather than live trading. The design-ahead rule (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`, cadence section) requires design to be Done >=2 sprints before the consuming FE story; E41 stories land in S18-S19, so research and wireframes run in **S16**.

Research is required because the review loop is genuinely new interaction (not a restyle of an existing screen): what does the owner actually do after a losing session, in what order, and what does "evidence" mean to them? Getting this wrong produces an analytics page nobody opens.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Research** with the two personas in `docs/plan/10-personas.md` who own this loop (Owner/principal trader, Account Manager): 3 moderated sessions, 45 min each, using the current spreadsheet/notes workflow as the baseline artefact.
- Research questions, at minimum: (a) what triggers a review session; (b) which fields are looked at first on a closed trade; (c) how tags are actually used (taxonomy vs free text); (d) whether demo results are considered meaningful; (e) what is exported and why.
- **Journey map** for "review yesterday's session" added to `docs/plan/17-ux-diagrams.md`.
- **Lo-fi wireframes** (Figma, `CandleViewer / E41 Journal` page) for SCR-093, SCR-094, SCR-095, SCR-096, each covering the states declared in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`: loading, empty, partial ("chart context unavailable"), reconciling, insufficient sample.
- **Information architecture** decision: `/journal` and `/journal/analytics` as separate routes with SCR-094 as page-or-drawer and SCR-096 as modal, consistent with `docs/plan/12-sitemap.md`.
- A written **findings memo** with 5-8 numbered findings, each mapped to a wireframe decision.

## Out of scope
- Hi-fi visuals, tokens, motion (E41-D02/D03).
- Any Figma work on replay (SCR-097+, owned by E26) or alerts (E40).
- Quantitative/analytics instrumentation studies - the sample size is one owner plus a few managers.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Research completed and synthesised
  Given 3 moderated sessions have been run and recorded with consent
  When the findings memo is published
  Then it contains at least 5 numbered findings, each traced to a specific wireframe decision on SCR-093, SCR-094, SCR-095 or SCR-096

Scenario: Every declared state is drawn
  When the CDO reviews the wireframe set
  Then every state listed for each screen in docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md exists as a frame, including the empty and "chart context unavailable" states
  And no frame introduces a component absent from docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md without an explicit new-component note

Scenario: Statistics are not presented as advice
  Given a wireframe shows expectancy or win rate
  Then the frame carries the low-sample caveat treatment and no prescriptive language ("you should...") anywhere on the surface
```

## Technical notes / design
Wireframes must honour two hard product constraints that emerged from the plan and are non-negotiable in review: DEMO and LIVE trades are **visibly separated and never aggregated** (SCR-093 sign-off checklist), and every chart has a **table alternative** (SCR-095 a11y note). Both are drawn at wireframe stage, not retrofitted at hi-fi.

## Test plan
N/A (design artefact). Validation is the moderated sessions themselves plus a CDO review; the wireframe set is re-validated by E41-D05 design QA against the built screens.

## Security notes
Session recordings contain real account identifiers and P&L. Recordings are stored in the private research drive, retained 90 days, and any screenshot used in the memo has account ids and balances redacted. No API keys or key identifiers may appear in any research artefact (asset A-12, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`).

## Accessibility notes
Wireframes annotate reading order, table semantics for SCR-093, and the "View as table" affordance for every chart on SCR-095. Density defaults chosen so that contrast can reach 4.5:1 at hi-fi (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` section on dense tables).

## Performance notes
Wireframes must assume server-side aggregation and cursor pagination - no design may imply the client holds 10 000 trades in memory to compute a total (SCR-093 performance note).

## Observability
Defines which analytics events the screens must emit: `journal.list_viewed`, `journal.filtered`, `journal.detail_viewed`, `journal.analytics_viewed`, `journal.analytics_filtered`, `journal.cohort_changed`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] 3 sessions run, notes and consent recorded.
- [ ] Findings memo published and linked from this ticket.
- [ ] Journey map merged into `docs/plan/17-ux-diagrams.md`.
- [ ] Wireframes for all four screens, all declared states, in Figma with a shareable link on the ticket.
- [ ] CDO review passed; sign-off comment recorded (design sign-off criterion).
- [ ] New-component candidates (CMP-166..169) flagged to the design-system team.

## Dependencies

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.
- **Design tooling**: *Figma* → **Penpot** (`docs/design/README.md`); frames on a page named after this ticket; exports via `docs/design/_tools/penpot_export.py`. Bind only to semantic tokens in `packages/ui/tokens/`.
- **Moderated usability / participant sessions** → a documented **heuristic evaluation** (Nielsen + the trading-specific heuristics in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`), a written session protocol ready for the owner to run later, and an **owner walkthrough** checklist posted on the issue. Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.
- **CVD / contrast validation** → computed programmatically (WCAG contrast matrix over the token JSON; CVD simulation via a documented script), attached as artefacts.
- **Spikes**: findings go to `docs/plan/spikes/<KEY>.md` via a normal PR (branch `spike/<epic>-<slug>`); any ADR named by the spike uses the **next free number** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (ADR-0001…0016 are taken).
- **Dependencies**: `blocked_by` now lists the concrete prerequisite tickets (not whole epics). Start when those are **merged** (In Test or Done).
- Anything that genuinely needs a human that is not the owner (external pen-test vendor, legal) stays as-is and is flagged `needs-owner` on the issue.

title: Hi-fi SCR-093 journal list and SCR-096 tag manager
body:
## Context
SCR-093 is the entry point to the whole journal area and the densest table in R3 after the positions grid; SCR-096 is the tag taxonomy's only editing surface and the place where a destructive merge/delete is confirmed. Both have explicit design sign-off checklists in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` that this ticket must satisfy item by item.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-093 hi-fi** (`/journal`), satisfying its checklist: columns (open/close time, symbol, side, size, entry, exit, P&L, R, fees, account, environment, tags, rating); DEMO and LIVE visibly separated and never aggregated; filters (date range, symbol, account, environment, tag, outcome); bulk tagging; totals row ("42 trades - win 57% - expectancy +0.34R - P&L +1,204"); empty state tied to recording/trading start; export affordance.
- **States**: loading, empty, partial ("chart context unavailable" for trades predating recording), reconciling (fills still arriving).

## Scope / Deliverables

- **MAE/MFE presentation**: price, USDT and R for each, plus the timestamp at which each occurred, and a `bar-derived` marker when only bar extremes were available (US-JRN-005).
- **SCR-095 hi-fi**, satisfying its checklist: the metric set (win rate, expectancy, avg R, profit factor, max drawdown with depth and duration labelled, streaks, by-symbol, by-hour-of-day, by-day-of-week, by-tag, by-account, by-rule/setup); DEMO excluded by default with an explicit toggle; a table alternative for every chart; the small-sample warning ("12 trades - not statistically meaningful"); date-range and cohort controls; empty state; R-distribution histogram; MAE/MFE scatter with outcome encoded by **shape** as well as colour; balance transfers marked on the equity curve and excluded from performance.
- **New design-system entries**: CMP-167 JournalEquityCurveChart (Default / WithDrawdown / TableViewToggle) and CMP-168 JournalStatsSummaryCard (Default).
- A one-page **statistics legend** design: every metric links to its formula (US-JRN-006 NFR requires a documented formula reference reachable from the UI; the content is authored in E41-T05).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin

  Given a breakdown bucket contains fewer than 5 trades

Scenario: Context unavailable
  Given the recorded market data covering a trade has been pruned

Scenario: Chart table alternative
  Given any chart on SCR-095

```

## Technical notes / design
Charts are lightweight (CMP-167 may reuse the series primitive CMP-181 in a minimal pane) and are not the WebGL engine; the design must not assume engine features like LOD or crosshair sync. The context chart on SCR-094 is fed by `GET /journal/trades/{journalTradeId}/context`, which returns a `coverage` descriptor - the design consumes that descriptor to render partial coverage honestly. Equity curve is derived from journal entries, never from wallet balance snapshots (US-JRN-007 NFR), so a transfer marker is an annotation, not a step in the series.

## Test plan
N/A (design artefact); verified by E41-D05 design QA and by the a11y audit in E41-Q03 (colour-blind simulation on the scatter, contrast on the histogram).

## Security notes
SCR-094 shows sibling accounts within a trade group; frames must show only legs the viewer is granted, and an ungranted leg is rendered as an explicit "not in your scope" row rather than silently omitted (which would misstate group P&L) - this constraint is carried into E41-X01's threat model.

## Accessibility notes
MAE/MFE and the SL path are described in text; the mini chart has a table alternative; every chart carries a text summary ("Expectancy +0.34R over 42 trades"); colour is never the sole encoding; drawer focus management specified for the SCR-094 drawer variant.

## Performance notes
SCR-095 is interactive <=800 ms for 10 000 trades with server-side aggregation; SCR-094's context window renders <=1.5 s or falls back to the "context not recorded" state. No design may require a client-side scan of the full trade set.

Under the design-ahead rule no frontend story in E41 may start until its design is Status=Done. This ticket is that gate: a dedicated accessibility design review across all four screens, the motion specification, and the handoff package engineering builds from in S18-S19.

## Scope / Deliverables

- **Keyboard map** for the journal area, added to the screen entries: list navigation, open detail, bulk select, apply tag, export, and the replay jump.
- **Motion spec**: row selection, drawer open/close for SCR-094, chart transition on filter change, and the "recomputing totals" affordance - all honouring `prefers-reduced-motion` with an explicit reduced variant per transition; durations and easing from `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` tokens, no bespoke curves.

```gherkin
Scenario: Contrast verified, not assumed

  Then each pair meets the ratio required by docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md and the measurements are attached to the ticket

Scenario: Reduced motion
  Given prefers-reduced-motion is set
  Then every specified transition has a defined reduced variant and none of them conveys information that is lost when motion is removed

Scenario: Handoff is self-sufficient
  When a frontend engineer opens the handoff package
  Then every string, token, component id, state and announcement text needed to build SCR-093..096 is present without asking the designer a question

Scenario: Gate
```

title: Spike: choose the analytics query tier (Postgres vs DuckDB/Parquet)
body:
## Context
`GET /journal/analytics` must return totals plus up to seven breakdowns (`symbol`, `tag`, `hour_of_day`, `day_of_week`, `side`, `account`, `setup`) and an equity curve at `trade | hour | day | week` granularity, server-computed, for up to 10 000 trades, with SCR-095 interactive within 800 ms and breakdown queries within 2 s (US-JRN-008 NFR). `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` gives two candidate tiers: Postgres 16 (C-storage, authoritative) and Parquet+DuckDB (C18, "cold archive, analytics, long replay"), and `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` already declares a `journal_trades/ ym=.../ part-*.parquet` cold layout and a "Unified journal: cold Parquet + live Postgres" query pattern.

Choosing wrongly is expensive in both directions: Postgres-only risks blowing the 2 s budget on wide `GROUP BY` with tag joins over long ranges; DuckDB-only introduces a freshness seam (a trade closed a minute ago must appear immediately) plus a second RBAC enforcement point, which is a security risk, not just an engineering cost. This spike decides, with numbers, before E41-T03 is written.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A benchmark harness under `services/api/journal/bench/` generating synthetic `journal_trades` + `journal_trade_tags` at 1k / 10k / 100k rows with realistic tag cardinality (~40 tags, ~3 tags/trade) and 6 accounts.
- Measure, for each tier and each row count, p50/p95 wall time for: (a) totals only; (b) totals + all seven breakdowns; (c) equity curve at `trade` granularity; (d) MAE/MFE scatter payload; (e) a filtered query (account + symbol + tag + date range).
- Measure the same with a **hybrid** shape: Postgres for ranges within the hot window, DuckDB over Parquet beyond it, unioned - including the cost and correctness of the boundary.
- Evaluate index options on Postgres (the existing `ix_jt_time`, `ix_jt_symbol`, `ix_jt_account`, `ix_jt_outcome`, `ix_jt_setup`; candidate covering index and a materialised daily rollup).
- Evaluate how RBAC account scoping is enforced in each tier (a DuckDB path must not bypass the `granted_accounts` scope).
- Output: **ADR-0016 "Journal analytics query tier"** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/`, with the decision, the measured evidence table, the rejected options and the freshness/consistency contract.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the production endpoint (E41-T03); any change to the hot/cold roll-off job (E16); backtesting analytics.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Decision is evidence-based
  When the spike closes
  Then ADR-0016 exists with a measured p50/p95 table for every tier x row-count x query combination listed in Scope
  And the chosen tier meets <=2 s for the full breakdown query at 10 000 trades on the reference dev machine

Scenario: Freshness contract stated
  Given the chosen design involves any non-authoritative store
  Then the ADR states the maximum staleness in seconds, how a just-closed trade becomes visible, and what the UI must display while a result is stale

Scenario: RBAC is not weakened
  Then the ADR shows how account scoping is enforced in the chosen tier and demonstrates a query that a Manager cannot widen to another account

Scenario: Timebox respected
  Given the spike exceeds 3 engineer-days
  Then it is closed with the best-supported recommendation and the residual uncertainty recorded as a risk on E41-T03 rather than running open-ended
```

## Technical notes / design
Reference machine: the WSL Ubuntu dev environment from `docs/plan/20-architecture.md`. Synthetic data must use `numeric(38,18)` columns as declared, since decimal aggregation cost is part of what is being measured - benchmarking with `double precision` would flatter Postgres and invalidate the result. Tag breakdowns require joining `journal_trade_tags`, which is the most expensive shape; measure it explicitly rather than extrapolating from the symbol breakdown.

Default hypothesis to test, not to assume: Postgres with a covering index is sufficient at 10k, and the DuckDB path only earns its keep beyond ~100k trades, which this single-owner deployment will not reach within R3-R5. If the evidence supports it, ADR-0016 records "Postgres only for now; the Parquet layout stays as the archive format" and E41-T03 ships one code path.

## Test plan
The harness is the test: it is committed, reproducible via `make bench-journal`, and its dataset generator is seeded so numbers are comparable across reruns. A regression run of the harness is folded into E41-Q02.

## Security notes
The spike must not use production or real demo data - synthetic only. The RBAC evaluation above is a required output because an analytics path that reads Parquet directly could otherwise sidestep the API's `granted_accounts` scoping (threat: horizontal escalation, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` section 10 authorisation testing).

N/A (backend spike).

Budgets under test: `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 13 (REST read p95 <150 ms), SCR-095 (interactive <=800 ms at 10 000 trades), US-JRN-008 NFR (breakdowns <=2 s at 10 000 trades).

Defines the metric `journal_analytics_query_seconds` (histogram, labelled by `group_by` cardinality and tier) that E41-T03 must emit.

- **Endpoints**: `GET /journal/trades` (cursor pagination via the shared `Cursor`/`Limit` params; filters `account_ids`, `symbol`, `side`, `tag[]`, `outcome`, `from`, `to`; returns `Page` of `JournalTrade`), `GET /journal/trades/{journalTradeId}` (returns `JournalTradeDetail`), `GET /journal/trades/{journalTradeId}/notes` (returns `Note[]`).
- **RBAC**: `x-rbac: { permissions: [journal:read], scope: granted_accounts }` enforced by the shared dependency chain (session -> scope -> rate limit -> validate, `docs/plan/20-architecture.md`); deny-by-default; an id outside the caller's grant returns `404`, never `403` with existence disclosure.
- Pydantic schemas mirroring the OpenAPI components `JournalTrade`, `JournalTradeDetail`, `JournalSide`, `Note`, with `Decimal` serialised as string.
- Seed fixture loader for the QA fixtures named in E41-Q01.

## Out of scope
- Writing entries (E41-T02), tags/notes writes and export (E41-T04), analytics (E41-T03), any UI.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Contract conformance
  When the contract test suite runs GET /journal/trades, GET /journal/trades/{id} and GET /journal/trades/{id}/notes against docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml
  Then every response validates with no undocumented field and no undocumented status code

Scenario: Account scoping
  Given a Manager granted account A only
  When they request a journal trade belonging to account B by its id
  Then the response is 404 and an authorisation-denied event is logged

Scenario: Cursor stability
  Given 10 000 entries and a page size of 100
  When a new entry is materialised between page 3 and page 4 requests
  Then paging through the full set yields every pre-existing entry exactly once with no skip or duplicate

Scenario: Migration is reversible and idempotent
  When the migration is applied, downgraded and re-applied on a database that already contains the notes table
  Then it succeeds each time and the resulting schema matches docs/plan/21-database-schema.md section 3.7 byte-for-byte on column types and constraint names
```

## Technical notes / design
Cursor is keyset pagination on `(opened_at DESC, id DESC)` served by `ix_jt_time` - never `OFFSET`, which is both slow and unstable under concurrent inserts. All monetary fields are `numeric(38,18)` in the database and `Decimal` in Python, serialised as JSON strings (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` constraint C3); never float. `is_aggregate` rows and leg rows are both returned by default with an `is_aggregate` discriminator so the client can pick a view; a `view=legs|aggregate|both` query parameter is **not** added here because it is not in the contract - if the UI needs it, the contract changes first.

Repository methods: `list_trades(scope, filters, cursor, limit)`, `get_trade(scope, id)`, `list_notes(scope, trade_id)`. The scope object comes from the shared dependency and is always applied in SQL (a `WHERE exchange_account_id = ANY(:granted)` predicate), never filtered in Python after fetching.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: filter combination -> SQL predicate mapping; cursor encode/decode incl. malformed cursor -> 400; Decimal serialisation; scope predicate always present (a test that asserts every repository query string contains the scope clause).
- **Contract**: schemathesis/openapi validation on all three endpoints, including the `401`/`403`/`404` responses.
- **Integration**: against a real Postgres with the migration applied; 10k-row fixture; keyset stability test with concurrent insert.
- **Migration**: upgrade/downgrade/upgrade cycle in CI; schema diff assertion against the DDL in the plan doc.
- Coverage target >=85% on `services/api/journal/`.

Asset A-12 (journal content, classification 2/2/1). Threats addressed: **IDOR** on `journalTradeId` (mitigated by scope-in-SQL + 404-not-403), **horizontal escalation** across managers (mitigated by `granted_accounts` scope), **information disclosure** through error messages (generic 404 body). Note content is returned as stored; rendering safety is the client's responsibility and is asserted in E41-T04 and E41-X02. Reviewed under label `security`.

List endpoint p95 <150 ms at 10 000 rows with a 100-row page (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 13); verified in E41-Q02. `EXPLAIN` plans for the list query must show an index scan on `ix_jt_time` (or the account/symbol index when those filters are present), never a sequential scan.

title: Build the trade materialiser with MAE/MFE and closed-pnl reconciliation
body:
## Context
This is the heart of the epic and the only place US-JRN-001 (Must), US-JRN-004 (Should) and US-JRN-005 (Should) are satisfied. The journal is *derived*: a `TradeMaterialiser` consumes the OMS execution stream and produces `journal_trades` rows - one per trade-group leg plus one `is_aggregate` row per group (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` section 3.7.1). US-JRN-001's NFR is uncompromising: *"entries derive from the execution stream, are idempotent, and survive restarts"*. A duplicated or lost entry corrupts every statistic downstream, which is why this carries risk R7.

It also owns the truth check: nightly reconciliation against `GET /executions/closed-pnl` (which mirrors Bybit `GET /v5/position/closed-pnl` and is described in the contract as *"backfilled nightly and used to seed journal entries"*).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **`TradeMaterialiser`** in `services/api/journal/materialiser.py`, subscribing to the OMS execution stream (M14) with a durable consumer offset persisted in Postgres so a restart resumes exactly where it stopped.
- **Round-trip grouping**: accumulate executions per `(exchange_account_id, symbol, position_idx)` into an open trade; close it when position quantity returns to zero; compute `avg_entry_price` / `avg_exit_price` as quantity-weighted averages across all constituent fills (US-JRN-001 "Partial fills and scale-outs"), `entry_qty`, `exit_qty`, `hold_seconds`, `fees_paid`, `funding_paid`, `realised_pnl` (`net_pnl` is generated by the database), `outcome`, `origin`, `origin_rule_id`.
- **Aggregate rows**: when a `trade_group_id` is present, write the N leg rows and exactly one `is_aggregate = true` row (enforced by `ux_jt_agg`) whose P&L is the sum of the legs and whose prices are quantity-weighted across legs.
- **Idempotency**: `ux_jt_leg` (unique on `trade_group_leg_id`) and a deterministic natural key for non-group trades; all writes are `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` inside one transaction per trade; replaying the same execution batch produces byte-identical rows.
- **External modification** (US-JRN-001): a position change with no corresponding local order is recorded in the trade timeline as an external action and the entry is flagged so the audit trail shows the app did not cause it.
- **R-multiple**: `r_multiple = net_pnl / initial_risk_usd`, where `initial_risk_usd` comes from the planned stop at entry (`planned_sl_price`, `planned_tp_price` captured from the OMS order intent); when no stop existed, `initial_risk_usd` and `r_multiple` are NULL and the UI must show "no planned risk" rather than 0.
- **MAE/MFE** (US-JRN-005): `max_adverse_price` / `max_favourable_price` computed **once at close** from recorded prices over the trade's lifetime, stored, and never recomputed on view; expressed downstream in price, USDT and R. When only bars exist for part of the window, compute from bar extremes and mark the values `bar-derived` (a flag on the entry) so analytics can exclude or caveat them.
- **Snapshot capture** (US-JRN-004): an **asynchronous**, best-effort capture of the configured views at entry and exit, written to object storage and referenced by `journal_trades.screenshot_path`. Capture must never sit in the order-submission path (US-JRN-004 NFR). On failure the trade is still journaled and the failure reason is recorded on the entry. A configurable storage budget prunes oldest non-pinned snapshots first, and the applied policy is stated on the entry.
- **`replay_anchor_ts`** set to entry time minus the configured lead, for the E41-S02 deep link.
- **Nightly reconciliation job** comparing each closed entry's `realised_pnl` and fees against `GET /executions/closed-pnl`; a divergence beyond one quantisation step increments `journal_reconciliation_divergence_total`, writes an audit entry and raises a `warning` alert; the entry is flagged `divergent` and the UI shows it rather than hiding it. Demo's 7-day order-history pruning is handled per `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md`: an order older than 7 days missing from history is `expired_from_history` and reconciled against the local record with `authoritative_source="local"`, not raised as a divergence.

## Out of scope
- Analytics aggregation (E41-T03); tags and notes (E41-T04); any UI; changing how the OMS emits executions (E29).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Scale-out grouped into one trade
  Given an entry of 1.0 BTC filled in three partials and an exit in two partials
  When the position reaches zero
  Then exactly one journal entry exists with quantity-weighted avg_entry_price and avg_exit_price and exit_qty equal to entry_qty

Scenario: Idempotent across restart
  Given the materialiser is killed after writing the entry but before committing its consumer offset
  When it restarts and replays the execution batch
  Then no duplicate entry is created and the existing row is byte-identical to before the restart

Scenario: Fan-out shape
  Given a trade group of three accounts closes
  Then three leg rows exist, each keyed by its trade_group_leg_id, plus exactly one is_aggregate row whose net_pnl equals the sum of the legs

Scenario: External close
  Given part of a position is closed on the Bybit web UI, outside CandleViewer
  Then the entry still closes correctly and the external action appears in the trade timeline marked as external

Scenario: Snapshot failure does not lose the trade
  Given snapshot capture raises an exception
  Then the journal entry is written, screenshot_path is null and the failure reason is recorded on the entry
  And order submission latency is unaffected

Scenario: MAE/MFE from bars only
  Given tick data for the first half of the trade has been pruned
  Then MAE and MFE are computed from bar extremes for that portion and the entry is flagged bar-derived

Scenario: Reconciliation divergence
  Given closed-pnl reports realised P&L differing from the local entry by more than one quantisation step
  Then the entry is flagged divergent, journal_reconciliation_divergence_total increments, an audit entry is written and a warning alert is raised

Scenario: Demo history pruning is not a divergence
  Given a demo order older than 7 days is absent from /v5/order/history
  Then it is treated as expired_from_history, reconciled against the local record with authoritative_source local, and no divergence alert is raised
```

## Technical notes / design
Money maths uses `Decimal` end to end and quantises with `ROUND_HALF_UP` at the declared scale (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` constraint C3 and the fee rules in section 12). Weighted average: `sum(price_i * qty_i) / sum(qty_i)` computed in `Decimal`, quantised only at the final assignment - never per-fill, which accumulates error.

Consumer design: at-least-once delivery from the bus plus database-level idempotency keys, rather than attempting exactly-once. Offset commit happens **after** the transaction commits, so the failure mode is redelivery (safe) and never loss.

Open-trade state lives in memory with a periodic checkpoint to Postgres; on restart, unclosed state is rebuilt by replaying executions since the last checkpoint rather than trusting the in-memory snapshot. Per `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` F8, journal writes buffer to a bounded on-disk WAL and replay on recovery when Postgres is unavailable.

Snapshot capture runs on a bounded work queue with a drop-oldest policy so a backlog can never apply back-pressure to the execution stream.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: weighted-average maths incl. Decimal edge cases; R-multiple with and without a planned stop; outcome classification incl. breakeven; MAE/MFE from ticks, from bars, and mixed; external-modification detection; budget pruning order.
- **Integration**: recorded Bybit execution fixtures (`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`) driving full open->scale->close cycles; fan-out group of three accounts; restart-mid-close idempotency test; WAL buffering with Postgres stopped and restarted.
- **Contract**: entries produced validate against the `JournalTrade` schema.
- **Chaos** (with E41-Q02): execution stream disconnect and replay; object storage unavailable during snapshot; Postgres unavailable for 60 s.
- **Property-based**: for any random sequence of fills summing to a flat position, exactly one entry is produced and `exit_qty == entry_qty`.
- Coverage target >=85%; this module is held to >=90% locally given R7.

## Security notes
Snapshots may contain account balances and open positions - they are stored in the private object store with the same classification as A-12 and are never served without a `journal:read` check scoped to the entry's account. The reconciliation job calls the exchange adapter with existing credentials only; it must not require any new API permission, and withdrawal permission remains OFF. The external-modification flag is security-relevant evidence (it distinguishes "the app did this" from "a human did this") and is written to the audit log.

## Accessibility notes
N/A (backend).

## Performance notes
Materialiser must keep `journal_materialiser_lag_seconds` p95 under 5 s at the R3 execution rate; snapshot capture is off the hot path by construction. The nightly reconciliation job must complete within 10 minutes for a full year of entries.

## Observability
Metrics `journal_entries_materialised_total{kind=leg|aggregate}`, `journal_materialiser_lag_seconds`, `journal_snapshot_failures_total{reason}`, `journal_reconciliation_divergence_total`, `journal_reconciliation_duration_seconds`. Audit events for external modification and for divergence. Structured logs carry `trade_group_id` and `journal_trade_id` for correlation.

body:
## Context
US-JRN-006 (Must), US-JRN-007 (Should) and US-JRN-008 (Should) are all served by one endpoint: `GET /journal/analytics`, described in the contract as *"Server-computed statistics for the Analytics screen: equity curve, win rate, expectancy, profit factor, average R, drawdown, and breakdowns by symbol, tag, session hour, day-of-week, side and account"*. Computation is server-side by requirement (SCR-093/095 performance notes) - the client never scans the trade set.

The subtle requirements are statistical, not technical: environments must never be mixed (US-JRN-006), a sample under 20 trades carries an explicit caveat, buckets under 5 trades are marked low-confidence (US-JRN-008), and balance transfers are marked on the equity curve but excluded from performance (US-JRN-007).

## Scope / Deliverables
- `JournalAnalyticsService` in `services/api/journal/analytics.py` implementing the tier chosen by ADR-0016 (E41-K01).
- **Endpoint** `GET /journal/analytics` with the contract's parameters: `account_ids`, `symbol`, `from`, `to`, `group_by[]` (`symbol | tag | hour_of_day | day_of_week | side | account | setup`), `equity_curve_interval` (`trade | hour | day | week`); RBAC `journal:read` scoped `granted_accounts`; returns `JournalAnalytics`.
- **Totals**: `trades`, `wins`, `losses`, `breakeven`, win rate, average win, average loss, expectancy in R, profit factor, average R, average hold time, max drawdown (depth **and** duration), streaks.
- **Equity curve** derived from journal entries (not wallet snapshots, US-JRN-007 NFR), at the requested interval, with drawdown envelope and balance-transfer markers that are annotations excluded from performance maths.
- **R-distribution histogram** with fixed, documented bucket edges so two queries are comparable.
- **MAE/MFE distribution** payload for the SCR-095 scatter, filterable by tag (US-JRN-005 "Aggregate view"), with `bar_derived` entries flagged so the client can caveat them.
- **Breakdowns**: each bucket returns count, win rate, expectancy, net P&L, and a `low_confidence: true` flag when count < 5.
- **Environment separation**: responses are always partitioned by `env` + `is_paper`; the service refuses to aggregate across environments - a request that would mix them returns per-environment result sets, and the response always states the active environment filter.
- **Low-sample flag**: `insufficient_sample: true` on the totals object when the matched count < 20.
- Response caching keyed by (scope, filters, max `updated_at` in range) with explicit invalidation when the materialiser writes, so a just-closed trade is never missing.

## Out of scope
- The dashboard UI (E41-S03); the formula reference document (E41-T05); export (E41-T04); backtesting statistics.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Documented statistics
  When totals are requested over a known fixture of 100 trades
  Then win rate, expectancy in R, profit factor, average win, average loss, max drawdown depth and duration match the values computed by hand in the fixture's expectation file exactly

Scenario: Environments are never mixed
  Given the range contains both live and demo entries
  When analytics are requested
  Then the response contains separate result sets per environment and no field aggregates across them

Scenario: Low sample
  Given 12 trades match the filter
  Then totals carry insufficient_sample true

Scenario: Low-confidence buckets
  Given a symbol bucket contains 4 trades
  Then that bucket carries low_confidence true

Scenario: Transfers excluded
  Given a balance transfer occurred inside the range
  Then it appears as a marker on the equity curve and does not change expectancy, profit factor or net P&L

Scenario: Freshness
  Given a trade closes and is materialised
  When analytics for a range covering it are requested
  Then it is included, regardless of any cached response

Scenario: Budget
  Given 10 000 entries and all seven breakdowns requested
  Then the response returns within 2 s and journal_analytics_query_seconds records the timing
```

## Technical notes / design
Expectancy in R = mean(`r_multiple`) over entries where `r_multiple` is non-null; entries without a planned stop are **excluded from R statistics and the exclusion count is reported**, rather than being silently treated as 0R - the latter would bias expectancy toward zero (risk R12). Profit factor = sum(positive `net_pnl`) / abs(sum(negative `net_pnl`)); when there are no losses it is reported as `null` with a reason, not as infinity. Max drawdown is computed on the equity series as the largest peak-to-trough decline, reporting both depth (absolute and %) and duration in seconds.

All aggregation is `Decimal`-safe: SQL `numeric` aggregation in Postgres, or DuckDB `DECIMAL` if ADR-0016 chose that tier. Any use of `float` inside the aggregation is permitted only for histogram bucketing and must be converted at the response boundary per `24-internal-schemas.md` C3.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: every formula against a hand-computed fixture; profit factor with zero losses; expectancy with null-R entries; drawdown on synthetic equity series with known answers; bucket edge behaviour at exactly 5 and exactly 20.
- **Contract**: response validates against `JournalAnalytics`; all `group_by` values exercised.
- **Integration**: 10k fixture, all breakdowns, timing asserted.
- **Regression**: a golden-file test on the full analytics response for `journal_fixture_10k` so an accidental formula change is loud.
- Coverage target >=85%.

## Security notes
Scope enforcement identical to E41-T01 (SQL-level `granted_accounts`); the caching key **includes the scope**, so a cached Owner response can never be served to a Manager - this is an explicit test, since scope-blind caching is the classic way an RBAC layer is defeated. No account identifiers beyond those in scope appear in breakdowns keyed by account.

## Accessibility notes
N/A (backend), but the response must carry the text summary inputs the UI needs (counts alongside every percentage) so SCR-095 can render "Expectancy +0.34R over 42 trades" without recomputation.

## Performance notes
Budgets: p95 <150 ms for the totals-only query; <=2 s for totals + seven breakdowns at 10 000 trades (US-JRN-008 NFR); measured in E41-Q02 against the E41-K01 harness.

## Observability
`journal_analytics_query_seconds{group_by_count,tier}`, `journal_analytics_cache_hits_total` / `_misses_total`, `journal_analytics_excluded_null_r_total`; analytics events emitted by the client, not here.

title: Implement tags, notes, auto-tagging and the audited export job
body:
## Context
This ticket carries the user-authored half of the journal - US-JRN-002 (Must, notes and tags), US-JRN-003 (Should, automatic tagging) and US-JRN-010 (Could, export) - plus their audit obligations. Journal writes are **audited**, not merely analytics (SCR-093: *"journal content is user-authored evidence and must be tamper-evident"*), and exports are the epic's highest-rated disclosure threat (S4 / SR-098, risk R13).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **`PATCH /journal/trades/{journalTradeId}`** writing only the user-authored fields the contract permits - `rating`, `tags`, `setup`, `mistakes`, `checklist`. Any attempt to write a computed field (`realised_pnl`, `r_multiple`, `mae_r`, `mfe_r`, durations) returns `422` naming the offending field; computed fields are never silently ignored.
- **`POST /journal/trades/{journalTradeId}/notes`** creating markdown notes with an optional chart snapshot reference (`NoteInput` -> `Note`), with **edit history retained** (US-JRN-002) - an edit writes a new revision rather than overwriting - and server-side sanitisation of the markdown (no raw HTML, no script URIs, no external image auto-fetch).
- **`GET /journal/tags`** (usage counts) and **`POST /journal/tags`** (create; unique on `lower(name)` per `ux_jtag_name`, `<=40` chars by contract, `<=24` by the SCR-096 validation rule - implement the stricter UI limit as a validation and document the contract's wider bound), plus rename / merge / delete server-side operations backing SCR-096.
- **Merge and rename are single transactions** with a reported affected-trade count, not client-side loops (SCR-096 performance note); renaming a tag used by 5 000 trades completes as one transaction.
- **Bulk tagging**: apply/remove a tag across a selected set, returning the count of affected trades (US-JRN-002 "Bulk tagging").
- **Auto-tagging** (US-JRN-003): on materialisation, apply provenance tags - the managing rule's name and version when a rule controlled the exit (`origin_rule_id`, closing the loop with the rule engine's `log_journal_tag` action), and detector-context tags when a detector fired within the configured window before entry. Auto tags are written with `journal_trade_tags.auto_applied = true`, carry provenance, **never overwrite manual tags**, and a user removal is *recorded* (an audit event plus a suppression record) so the tag does not silently reappear on reprocessing.
- **Export** (US-JRN-010): CSV (one row per trade, documented column semantics) and Parquet over the filtered set; role-scoped **server-side**; watermarked with the exporting identity and timestamp (SR-098); audited; **never** containing API keys, key identifiers, secrets or internal ids beyond the journal trade id. Above 50 000 matched rows the export runs asynchronously and notifies on completion via the E40 notification channel.

## Out of scope
- Tag manager UI (E41-S04); export UI affordance (E41-S04); the analytics payload (E41-T03); the rule engine itself (E35).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Computed fields are not writable
  When a PATCH attempts to set realised_pnl
  Then the response is 422 naming realised_pnl and the stored entry is unchanged

Scenario: Note sanitisation and history
  When a note containing a script tag and an onerror attribute is submitted
  Then the stored content has them removed, the note renders safely, and a subsequent edit creates a new revision with the previous revision retained

Scenario: Audited writes
  When a tag is added, a tag is removed, a rating is set or a trade is excluded
  Then an audit entry is written with actor, subject and before/after values, and it is present in the append-only audit log

Scenario: Tag merge
  Given a tag applied to 5000 trades is merged into another
  Then the operation completes in a single transaction, reports affectedTrades 5000, and writes journal.tag_merged with that count

Scenario: Auto tag provenance and removal
  Given a rule managed the exit and an auto tag was applied
  When the user removes that auto tag
  Then the removal is recorded and reprocessing the same trade does not re-add the tag

Scenario: Auto tags never overwrite manual ones
  Given a manual tag with the same name exists
  Then auto-tagging leaves the manual tag intact and does not downgrade its provenance

Scenario: Export scoping
  Given a Manager with access to one account exports the journal
  Then the file contains only that account's trades, enforced server-side, is watermarked with the exporter's identity and timestamp, and is recorded in the audit log

Scenario: Export contains no secrets
  When any export is produced
  Then no API key, key identifier, credential or exchange account secret appears in any column, asserted by an automated scan of the output

Scenario: Large export
  Given 60 000 rows match
  Then the export is generated asynchronously and the user is notified when it is ready
```

## Technical notes / design
Sanitisation uses an allowlist markdown renderer server-side (store sanitised, render sanitised - defence in depth rather than trusting the client). Note revisions live in the `notes` table's history mechanism with `subject_kind = 'journal_trade'`, validated by `trg_notes_subject`.

Auto-tag suppression is a small table keyed `(journal_trade_id, journal_tag_id)` recording the user's removal, checked before any auto-apply. Without it, "auto tags editable" (US-JRN-003) is not actually true because reprocessing would undo the user's decision.

CSV column semantics are documented in the same reference E41-T05 produces, so an exported file is interpretable without the app. Watermark: a header comment row in CSV and file-level metadata in Parquet, both carrying exporting user, timestamp, applied filters and the account scope.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: field-allowlist enforcement; sanitiser against an XSS payload corpus; tag name uniqueness case-insensitively; merge transaction counts; suppression logic; watermark content.
- **Contract**: PATCH/POST endpoints against the OpenAPI schemas incl. `409` on duplicate tag.
- **Integration**: 5 000-trade merge in one transaction; async export path above the 50k threshold incl. the notification.
- **Security**: an automated secret-scan assertion over generated exports; a cross-manager export attempt asserted to return only in-scope rows.
- **E2E** (with E41-Q01): bulk tag from SCR-093, merge from SCR-096, export and download.
- Coverage target >=85%.

## Security notes
Directly mitigates **S4** (journal exports contain account identifiers shared across managers) via **SR-098**: role-scoped, watermarked, audited exports. Additional threats handled: stored XSS via notes (sanitisation server-side), tampering with evidence (audited writes + note revision history + computed fields immutable), auto-tag forgery (provenance flag distinguishes auto from manual so a manual tag cannot be passed off as rule-derived). Data classification A-12. **This ticket requires the `security` review label and is an input to E41-X02.**

## Accessibility notes
N/A (backend); the error messages returned (e.g. the `422` field name, the affected-trade count) are surfaced verbatim by the UI, so they are written as user-facing copy, not developer strings.

## Performance notes
Tag merge/rename must be O(1) round-trips regardless of usage count; export streams rather than materialising the full set in memory; async threshold at 50 000 rows.

## Observability
`journal_export_rows_total{format}`, `journal_export_duration_seconds`, `journal_tag_operations_total{op}`, `journal_autotag_applied_total`, `journal_autotag_suppressed_total`; audit events `journal.note_added`, `journal.tag_added`, `journal.tag_removed`, `journal.trade_excluded`, `journal.rating_set`, `journal.tag_created`, `journal.tag_renamed`, `journal.tag_merged`, `journal.tag_deleted` (with `affectedTrades`), `journal.exported`.

title: Author the journal statistics formula reference and ADR-0016 follow-up
body:
## Context
US-JRN-006's NFR is explicit: *"all statistics are defined in a documented formula reference available from the UI"*. This is not documentation hygiene - it is the control that keeps risk R12 in check. A win rate whose denominator is undefined, or an expectancy that silently treats stopless trades as 0R, is a number that misleads its only reader. This ticket authors that reference and links it from SCR-095.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `docs/plan/25-journal-statistics-reference.md` (new) documenting, for every statistic returned by `GET /journal/analytics`: the plain-English definition, the exact formula, the population (which entries are included and which excluded and why), the units, the edge cases, and a worked example against the shipped `journal_fixture_100` fixture.
- Statistics covered: trade count, win / loss / breakeven counts, win rate, average win, average loss, expectancy in R, profit factor, average R, average hold time, max drawdown (depth absolute and %, duration), streaks, R-distribution bucket edges, MAE, MFE (price, USDT, R; and what `bar-derived` means), equity curve construction and the treatment of balance transfers.
- Explicit statements of the three decisions that most affect interpretation: (1) entries with no planned stop are excluded from R statistics and the exclusion count is reported; (2) profit factor with zero losses is `null`, not infinity; (3) environments are never aggregated.
- The **CSV export column dictionary** for US-JRN-010 ("documented column semantics"), in the same document so an exported file is interpretable standalone.
- The low-sample and low-confidence thresholds (20 trades; 5 per bucket) stated with their rationale.
- A UI entry point: the reference is reachable from SCR-095 (a "How these are calculated" link), specified with E41-D03's statistics legend.
- Update `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0029-journal-analytics-query-tier.md` with the as-built outcome if implementation diverged from the spike's recommendation.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the statistics (E41-T03); rendering the legend (E41-S03); backtesting metrics.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every returned statistic is documented
  When the JournalAnalytics response schema is enumerated
  Then every numeric field in it has an entry in docs/plan/25-journal-statistics-reference.md with formula, population, units and edge cases

Scenario: Worked example matches the implementation
  When the worked example is recomputed against journal_fixture_100 by the test suite
  Then every documented value matches the endpoint's output exactly, and the test fails if either drifts

Scenario: Export is self-describing
  Given a CSV export and the reference document
  Then every column is defined, including units, sign convention and null semantics
```

## Context
SCR-093 (`/journal`) is the entry point to the journal area and delivers the visible half of US-JRN-001 (Must), US-JRN-002 (Must), US-JRN-003 (Should) and the list-side of US-JRN-008 (Should). It is a dense, virtualised table over 10 000+ entries where the two non-negotiables are that **demo and live are never aggregated** and that **aggregate statistics come from the server**, never from a client-side scan.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Route `/journal` in `apps/web/src/routes/journal/`, guarded by `journal:read`.
- **Table** built on CMP-049 with virtualisation; columns: open/close time, symbol, side, size, entry, exit, P&L (CMP-116 PnLBadge), R-multiple, fees, account, environment, tags (CMP-169 TagEditor inline), rating. Rows rendered via **CMP-166 JournalEntryRow** (new component: variants Winner, Loser, WithRuleTag, WithManualTags).
- **Filters** via CMP-055 FilterBar + CMP-047 DateRangePicker: date range, symbol, account (multi), environment, tag, outcome - each mapped to the `GET /journal/trades` query parameters (`account_ids`, `symbol`, `side`, `tag[]`, `outcome`, `from`, `to`).
- **Environment separation**: demo and live entries are rendered in visibly separate, individually totalled groups; no combined total is ever rendered across them; the active environment filter is always displayed.
- **Server-side totals row** ("42 trades - win 57% - expectancy +0.34R - P&L +1,204") sourced from `GET /journal/analytics` totals for the active filter, with the designed "recomputing" affordance while it refreshes.
- **Cursor pagination / infinite virtual scroll** over the `Page` envelope with `next_cursor`.
- **Bulk selection and bulk tagging** through the E41-T04 bulk endpoint, reporting the affected-trade count.
- **Row actions**: open detail (E41-S02), open in replay, edit tags, exclude from analytics (audited), set rating.
- **States** per the screen entry: loading, empty ("No trades in this range", tied to recording/trading start with the recorder CTA for the Owner per the catalogue's empty-state convention), partial ("chart context unavailable" for trades predating recording), reconciling (fills still arriving), and the `divergent` flag from E41-T02 surfaced rather than hidden.
- Analytics events `journal.list_viewed`, `journal.filtered`, `journal.exported`; audited actions routed through the API so the audit entry is server-written.

## Out of scope
- Trade detail (E41-S02), analytics dashboard (E41-S03), tag manager modal (E41-S04); the export *job* (E41-T04) - this screen only triggers it.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Listing and filtering
  Given 10 000 journal entries exist across two accounts
  When I filter to one account, one symbol and the last 30 days
  Then only matching entries are listed, the filter chips reflect the selection, and the totals row recomputes from the server for that filter

Scenario: Environments are never aggregated
  Given the range contains both demo and live entries
  Then they render as separate groups with separate totals and no combined figure appears anywhere on the screen

Scenario: Bulk tagging
  Given I select 12 entries
  When I apply the tag "absorption"
  Then the server applies it, the UI reports "12 trades updated", and the tag becomes available as a filter

Scenario: Auto tags are distinguishable and protected
  Given an entry carries a rule-sourced auto tag
  Then it renders visually distinct from manual tags and cannot be removed by the inline editor's manual-tag control

Scenario: Empty state
  Given no trades exist in the selected range
  Then the empty state states the fact, its cause, one primary action and a learn-more link, following the CMP-026 anatomy

Scenario: Loading and error
  Given the journal API returns 503
  Then an error state with a retry action is shown, no partial or stale totals are displayed as if current

Scenario: Scoping
  Given I am a Manager granted one account
  Then the account filter offers only that account and no entry outside my grant is listed or countable

Scenario: Density budget
  Given 10 000 rows are loaded
  When I scroll continuously for 5 seconds
  Then scripting time stays at or below 8 ms per frame
```

## Technical notes / design
Build against the signed-off hi-fi and handoff package from E41-D02/E41-D04; every string comes from the approved copy deck, every colour and spacing from tokens. Data fetching uses the shared query client with the cursor envelope; the totals request is a separate, debounced call so a slow aggregate never blocks the row list from painting. Sorting is server-side (it must be, given pagination) - a client-side sort over a partial page would be a lie.

`is_aggregate` rows and leg rows both arrive from the API; the default view shows aggregate rows for trade groups with legs expandable inline, so a fan-out trade reads as one trade by default.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: filter state -> query param mapping; environment grouping logic; totals debounce; auto-tag read-only enforcement; cursor append without duplication.
- **Component/Storybook**: CMP-166 variants; empty, loading, error, partial, reconciling, divergent states; axe on each story.
- **E2E (Playwright, with E41-Q01)**: close a trade on demo -> it appears in the list; filter; bulk tag; open detail; export.
- **Perf**: 10k-row virtualised scroll benchmark asserting <=8 ms scripting per frame.
- **a11y**: axe-core CI on the route; keyboard-only pass (navigate, sort, select, bulk tag, open detail).
- Coverage target >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
The account filter is populated from the user's grant, never from a full account list. All audited actions (`journal.tag_added`, `journal.tag_removed`, `journal.rating_set`, `journal.trade_excluded`) are performed via the API so the audit record is server-authored and cannot be spoofed by the client. Note and tag content rendered here is already sanitised server-side (E41-T04) and is additionally rendered as text, never as HTML.

## Accessibility notes
Table semantics with sortable headers announcing sort state; R and P&L always signed and unit-labelled; bulk-selection count announced via a live region; tag chips reachable and removable by keyboard; the announcement strings are those authored in E41-D04. Virtualisation must not break `aria-rowcount` / `aria-rowindex`.

## Performance notes
10 000 rows scroll without exceeding 8 ms scripting per frame; aggregate stats server-side only (SCR-093 performance note); initial route interactive well inside the page budget with the first page of 100 rows.

Emits `journal.list_viewed`, `journal.filtered`, `journal.exported`; client error boundary reports to the frontend error channel with `request_id` correlation.

title: Build the trade detail / post-mortem screen SCR-094 with replay deep-link
body:
## Context
SCR-094 delivers US-JRN-002 (notes/tags on a trade), US-JRN-004 (snapshots), US-JRN-005 (MAE/MFE) and US-JRN-009 (replay-linked post-mortem). It is where a trade is actually understood, and its hardest requirement is honesty about missing data: when retention has pruned the market context, the screen must say so and offer bar-level review, never spin (risk R15).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Page/drawer at `/journal/:journalTradeId` (drawer variant via CMP-046 when opened from SCR-093), guarded by `journal:read`.
- **Header**: symbol, side, size, account, environment, entry/exit price and time, R-multiple, net P&L (CMP-116).
- **Fills timeline** (CMP-049): time, price, qty, fee, fee currency, liquidity (maker/taker), order id, trade group, causing rule if any, and external-action rows marked as external (from E41-T02).
- **Attribution**: for every action taken on the trade, whether it was manual, an algo, or a named rule (with version).
- **MAE/MFE** shown in price, USDT and R with the timestamp of each extreme, and the `bar-derived` marker when applicable; described in text as well as drawn.
- **Fees and funding** broken out; `fee_estimated` entries flagged per the paper-matcher rule.
- **Trade-group siblings** row ("group Scalp x3: Main +65.0 | sub_001 +26.0 | sub_002 -3.0"); a leg outside the viewer's grant renders as an explicit "not in your scope" row rather than being omitted.
- **Context chart** fed by `GET /journal/trades/{journalTradeId}/context` (bars + footprint + own fills, `pad_seconds` default 900), honouring the returned `coverage` descriptor; entry/exit markers and the SL path drawn; a **table alternative** for the chart.
- **"Context not recorded" state** when coverage is absent: names what is missing, why (retention), and offers bar-level review if bars remain.
- **Snapshots** (US-JRN-004) displayed when present; when capture failed, the reason is shown rather than a broken image.
- **Notes and tags** editing via CMP-058 InlineEdit and CMP-169 TagEditor against the E41-T04 endpoints, with edit history visible.
- **"Open in replay"** (US-JRN-009) deep-linking into E26's replay at `replay_anchor_ts` (entry minus the configured lead) with the user's executions marked; when the recorded data is pruned, the action explains what is unavailable and offers bar-level replay if bars remain. Notes added during a replay review attach to the same journal entry.
- **"Open chart at entry"** and **export** (CMP-099 PrintExportBar).
- Analytics/audit events: `journal.detail_viewed`, `journal.note_added` (audited server-side), `journal.screenshot_exported`, `journal.replay_from_trade`.

## Out of scope
- The replay engine and its screens (E26); the snapshot capture pipeline (E41-T02); analytics aggregates (E41-S03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Full post-mortem renders
  Given a closed trade with five fills across two orders managed by a rule
  When I open its detail
  Then all five fills, their fees and liquidity flags, the managing rule name and version, MAE/MFE in price, USDT and R, and the context chart render within 1.5 s

Scenario: Context pruned
  Given the recorded tick data covering the trade has been deleted by retention
  Then the "context not recorded" state is shown naming what is missing, bar-level review is offered if bars remain, and no indefinite spinner appears

Scenario: Replay jump
  When I choose "replay this trade"
  Then replay opens at entry minus the configured lead time with my executions marked
  And notes I add during that review attach to this same journal entry

Scenario: Replay unavailable
  Given the recorded data for the trade has been pruned
  When I choose "replay this trade"
  Then the action explains precisely what is unavailable and offers bar-level replay if bars remain, instead of failing silently

Scenario: Out-of-scope sibling leg
  Given the trade group includes a leg on an account I am not granted
  Then that leg is shown as "not in your scope" and the group total states that it is partial

Scenario: Snapshot capture failed
  Given snapshot capture failed at entry
  Then the screen states the failure reason and the rest of the post-mortem renders normally

Scenario: Bar-derived excursions
  Given MAE/MFE were computed from bar extremes
  Then both values carry the bar-derived marker in text, not only as an icon
```

## Technical notes / design
One request paints the context (`/context` returns bars, footprint and fills together, explicitly so the review chart does not issue a burst of market-data requests). The chart is the lightweight primitive, not the full WebGL engine. The `coverage` descriptor drives the partial/absent states - never infer coverage from a short series, which would silently misrepresent a gap as an early start.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: coverage descriptor -> state mapping (full / partial / absent); MAE/MFE unit conversion; sibling-leg scoping; replay anchor computation.
- **Component/Storybook**: full, partial-coverage, no-coverage, snapshot-failed, bar-derived, out-of-scope-sibling, fee-estimated states; axe on each.
- **E2E**: open from SCR-093, add a note, add a tag, jump to replay, return; pruned-context path with a fixture whose recording was deleted.
- **a11y**: keyboard pass incl. drawer focus trap and return focus; screen-reader pass asserting the MAE/MFE and SL-path text descriptions and the chart table alternative.
- Coverage target >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
Enforces nothing itself - scoping is server-side - but must not leak the existence of out-of-scope data beyond the agreed "not in your scope" row (a deliberate, reviewed disclosure so group totals are not silently wrong; recorded in E41-X01's model). Note content is rendered as sanitised text; snapshots are fetched through the authenticated API, never from a public URL.

## Accessibility notes
MAE/MFE and the SL path described in text; the mini chart has a table alternative; drawer focus management per E41-D04; all numeric values signed and unit-labelled; the timeline is a semantic table.

## Performance notes
Context window renders <=1.5 s or falls back to the "context not recorded" state rather than a spinner (SCR-094 performance note).

title: Build the journal analytics dashboard SCR-095
body:
## Context
SCR-095 (`/journal/analytics`) delivers US-JRN-006 (Must), US-JRN-007 (Should), US-JRN-008 (Should) and the export entry point for US-JRN-010 (Could). Its defining constraint is epistemic: every number must be honest about its sample. A confident expectancy over 12 trades is the epic's main way of doing harm (risk R12), so the low-sample and low-confidence treatments are acceptance criteria, not polish.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Route `/journal/analytics` guarded by `journal:read`, fed entirely by `GET /journal/analytics` - **no client-side aggregation of the trade set**.
- **Summary tiles** via **CMP-168 JournalStatsSummaryCard** (new): win rate, expectancy in R, average R, profit factor, average hold time, max drawdown (depth and duration), current and best streaks, trade count.
- **Equity curve** via **CMP-167 JournalEquityCurveChart** (new) with drawdown overlay, maximum drawdown marked and its depth and duration labelled, balance-transfer markers shown and excluded from performance, and a `TableViewToggle` rendering the same points through CMP-049.
- **R-distribution histogram** with the documented bucket edges from E41-T05.
- **MAE/MFE scatter** for stop-quality review, outcome encoded by **shape as well as colour**, filterable by tag, with `bar-derived` points flagged.
- **Breakdown tables**: by symbol, tag, hour of day, day of week, side, account and setup/rule-source - each with count alongside P&L, sortable by any column, buckets with fewer than 5 trades visually **and textually** marked low-confidence.
- **Cohort controls**: date range (CMP-047), account multi-select, symbol, tag, and the environment toggle - **DEMO excluded by default** with an explicit toggle, and the active environment filter always displayed.
- **Low-sample treatment**: when fewer than 20 trades match, every headline statistic carries the caveat attached to the number, not only a page banner.
- **"How these are calculated"** link opening the reference authored in E41-T05.
- **Export** (CMP-099 PrintExportBar) triggering the E41-T04 job, with the async path above 50 000 rows showing a "we'll notify you" state.
- **States**: loading, empty, insufficient sample.
- Analytics events `journal.analytics_viewed`, `journal.analytics_filtered`, `journal.analytics_exported`, `journal.cohort_changed`.

## Out of scope
- Computing any statistic client-side; the formula reference content (E41-T05); trade list and detail (E41-S01/S02).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Dashboard renders within budget
  Given 10 000 journal entries match the filter
  When I open /journal/analytics
  Then the page is interactive within 800 ms and every statistic came from the server

Scenario: Demo excluded by default
  Given both live and demo entries exist
  When the page loads
  Then demo entries are excluded, the environment toggle shows this, and enabling demo renders it as a separate population rather than merging it into the live figures

Scenario: Low sample
  Given 12 trades match
  Then each headline statistic displays with the low-sample caveat attached to it, and the page does not present the figures as conclusive

Scenario: Low-confidence bucket
  Given the "hour 03" bucket contains 4 trades
  Then that row is marked low-confidence in text as well as visually

Scenario: Table alternative
  Given any chart on the page
  When I activate "View as table" using only the keyboard
  Then the same data renders as an accessible table with a text summary such as "Expectancy +0.34R over 42 trades"

Scenario: Transfers annotated not counted
  Given a balance transfer occurred in the range
  Then it is marked on the equity curve and none of the performance statistics change because of it

Scenario: Large export
  Given 60 000 rows match and I export
  Then the UI states the export is being prepared and that I will be notified, rather than appearing to hang
```

## Technical notes / design
One request per cohort change, debounced, with the `group_by[]` set matching the visible breakdowns so the server does not materialise breakdowns nobody is looking at. The response carries counts alongside percentages precisely so the text summaries need no client-side maths. Charts are the lightweight primitives (CMP-167 may reuse the series primitive CMP-181 in a minimal pane), not the WebGL engine.

Each chart's table alternative renders the identical data array the chart consumed - not a re-fetch and not a rounded copy - so the two can never disagree.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: cohort state -> query params; low-sample and low-confidence threshold rendering at exactly 20 and exactly 5; transfer markers excluded from displayed totals; table-alternative data identity with the chart's series.
- **Component/Storybook**: CMP-167 (Default, WithDrawdown, TableViewToggle) and CMP-168 (Default); empty, loading, insufficient-sample states; axe on each.
- **E2E**: filter by tag and account, toggle demo, switch every chart to its table, export.
- **Perf**: 10k-entry fixture, time-to-interactive asserted <=800 ms (E41-Q02).
- **a11y**: axe-core; colour-blind simulation on the scatter and histogram; screen-reader pass on the text summaries.
- Coverage target >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
Account breakdowns show only granted accounts; the export button respects the same scope and the server re-enforces it (SR-098). No statistic may be computed from a client-side cache that predates a scope change - the query key includes the scope so a grant revocation invalidates it.

## Accessibility notes
Every chart has a table alternative and a text summary; colour never the sole encoding (scatter uses shape by outcome); small buckets marked in text; headline numbers signed and unit-labelled; charts have accessible names and descriptions.

## Performance notes
Interactive <=800 ms for 10 000 trades; breakdown query <=2 s (US-JRN-008 NFR); no client-side scan of the trade set at any point.

`journal.analytics_viewed`, `journal.analytics_filtered`, `journal.analytics_exported`, `journal.cohort_changed`; client timing reported against the 800 ms budget.
