title: Build the journal tag manager SCR-096 and the export flow UI
body:
## Context
SCR-096 is the tag taxonomy's only editing surface (US-JRN-002 Must, US-JRN-003 Should) and the place where destructive operations - merge and delete - are confirmed against a stated affected-trade count. This story also ships the user-facing export flow for US-JRN-010 (Could), whose disclosure risk (R13, threat S4) is why the confirmation copy must state exactly what leaves the system.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Tag manager modal** (CMP-043 Dialog) reachable from SCR-093 and SCR-095: a table (CMP-049) of tags with name, colour, category, usage count and description.
- **Create / rename / merge / delete** flows against the E41-T04 endpoints, with CMP-058 InlineEdit for rename and CMP-044 ConfirmDialog for destructive operations.
- **Validation**: unique names (case-insensitive), <=24 characters per the screen's validation rule; category from `setup | mistake | emotion | session | general` matching `journal_tags.category`.
- **Merge/delete confirmation** restating the exact number of affected trades before the operation and reporting the result after; operations are server-side with progress, never a client-side loop.
- **Colour picker** whose output is validated for contrast in both themes, with colour always paired with the tag's text label.
- **Auto-tag rules** display: tags carrying an `auto_rule` predicate are shown as such and their provenance explained; auto-applied tags on trades are read-only in the manual editor.
- **Empty state** (CMP-026).
- **Export flow UI**: format choice (CSV / Parquet), a summary of exactly what will be exported (row count, date range, accounts in scope, columns), the watermark notice ("this file is watermarked with your identity and the export time and the export is recorded in the audit log"), the synchronous download path, and the asynchronous path above 50 000 rows with a "we'll notify you when it's ready" state and a link to the notification centre.
- Analytics/audit events `journal.tag_created`, `journal.tag_renamed`, `journal.tag_merged`, `journal.tag_deleted` (with `affectedTrades`), `journal.exported` - all server-written.

## Out of scope
- The tag/merge/export server logic (E41-T04); the notification channel (E40); the analytics dashboard (E41-S03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Create and rename
  When I create a tag "absorption" in category setup and later rename it to "absorption-reclaim"
  Then both operations succeed, the usage count is preserved, and the rename is reported as a single server-side operation

Scenario: Duplicate name
  When I create a tag whose name differs only by case from an existing one
  Then the form rejects it with a clear message and no request creates a duplicate

Scenario: Merge confirmation
  Given a tag applied to 5 000 trades
  When I merge it into another
  Then the confirmation states "5,000 trades will be affected", the operation runs server-side with progress, and the result restates the count

Scenario: Delete confirmation
  When I delete a tag used by 120 trades
  Then the confirmation restates that 120 trades lose the tag, and cancelling changes nothing

Scenario: Auto tags are protected
  Given a tag is applied automatically by a rule
  Then it is shown as auto with its provenance and cannot be removed through the manual tag control

Scenario: Export discloses its scope
  When I open the export flow as a Manager granted one account
  Then the summary names that account only, states the row count and date range, and states that the file is watermarked and audited

Scenario: Large export
  Given 60 000 rows match
  Then the flow switches to the asynchronous path, states that I will be notified, and does not block the UI

Scenario: Colour contrast
  When I pick any offered tag colour
  Then the paired label meets 4.5:1 in both themes and the picker rejects or warns on any value that does not
```

## Technical notes / design
The modal is a focus-trapped dialog with return focus to its invoker. The affected-trade count shown in a confirmation is fetched immediately before the confirmation renders (not cached from the list) so the number a user confirms against is current. Export summary figures come from the same filter the user is currently viewing, so "what will be exported" and "what I can see" are provably the same set.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: name validation incl. case-insensitive collision and the 24-char limit; confirmation copy interpolation with thousands separators; export threshold branching at exactly 50 000; auto-tag read-only enforcement.
- **Component/Storybook**: tag table populated and empty; merge/delete confirmations; colour picker in both themes; export flow sync and async variants; axe on each.
- **E2E**: create, rename, merge, delete a tag end to end; export as Owner and as Manager verifying scope copy; async export notification.
- **a11y**: keyboard-only pass through the modal and the export flow; focus trap and return focus; screen-reader announcement of the affected-trade count.
- Coverage target >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
Directly user-facing mitigation for threat **S4** / control **SR-098**: the export flow must state the scope, the watermark and the audit before the user confirms. The UI never constructs the export itself and never widens the filter beyond what the server will honour. Tag names are user input rendered as text, never as HTML.

## Accessibility notes
Tag list is a table with name, colour, usage count and description; colour is always paired with the tag's text label; merge/rename dialogs restate the affected trade count in text; modal focus trap and return focus; all controls keyboard reachable.

## Performance notes
Tag operations are server-side; renaming a tag used by 5 000 trades completes as a single transaction with progress rather than a client-side loop (SCR-096 performance note).

## Observability
Client emits `journal.exported` analytics; all tag mutations are audited server-side with `affectedTrades`.

## Context
Three budgets in the plan are only claims until measured: REST reads p95 <150 ms (`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 13), SCR-095 interactive <=800 ms at 10 000 trades, breakdown queries <=2 s at 10 000 trades (US-JRN-008 NFR), and SCR-093 scrolling at <=8 ms scripting per frame. Separately, `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` mandates chaos/failover tests, and the journal has a specific failure mode worth rehearsing: the materialiser losing or duplicating an entry across a restart or a Postgres outage would corrupt every downstream statistic (risk R7).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **k6 load scripts** under `tests/load/journal/`: `list_trades.js` (cursor paging at 100/page over 10k entries), `analytics_totals.js`, `analytics_all_breakdowns.js` (all seven `group_by` values), `trade_detail.js`, `trade_context.js`. Each reports p50/p95/p99 and error rate against the declared budget and fails the run on breach.
- **Frontend perf benchmarks**: SCR-093 virtualised scroll (scripting ms/frame over a 5 s continuous scroll at 10k rows) and SCR-095 time-to-interactive at 10k trades, both recorded as numbers in the ticket and wired as CI performance checks.
- **Export load**: 60 000-row CSV and Parquet exports, measuring duration, memory ceiling (must stream, not materialise) and that the async path engages.
- **Materialiser throughput**: replay a recorded execution burst and assert `journal_materialiser_lag_seconds` p95 <5 s.
- **Chaos scenarios** (each asserting both correctness and recovery):
  1. kill the API mid-close, restart -> exactly one entry, byte-identical (idempotency);
  2. Postgres unavailable for 60 s during active trading -> writes buffer to the bounded WAL and replay on recovery with no loss or duplication (`20-architecture.md` F8);
  3. execution stream disconnect and redelivery of an already-processed batch -> no duplicates;
  4. object storage unavailable during snapshot capture -> trades still journaled, failure reason recorded, no back-pressure on the execution stream;
  5. exchange 5xx / rate-limit 10018 during the nightly reconciliation -> job backs off, retries, and reports incomplete rather than reporting false divergences;
  6. clock skew of +/-2 s between the app and exchange timestamps -> trade grouping and hour-of-day breakdowns remain correct or degrade explicitly.
- A **results report** with the measured numbers against each budget, attached to this ticket and summarised for the R3 PRR.

## Out of scope
- Functional E2E (E41-Q01); a11y audit (E41-Q03); tuning work itself (defects are filed against the owning ticket).

```gherkin

Scenario: Frontend budgets met
  When SCR-093 is scrolled continuously for 5 seconds over 10 000 rows
  Then scripting time stays at or below 8 ms per frame
  And SCR-095 is interactive within 800 ms for the same dataset

Scenario: Idempotency under crash
  Given the API is killed between writing an entry and committing its consumer offset
  When it restarts and the batch is redelivered
  Then exactly one entry exists and it is byte-identical to the pre-crash row

Scenario: Postgres outage
  Given Postgres is unavailable for 60 seconds while trades close
  Then journal writes buffer to the bounded WAL and replay on recovery with no lost or duplicated entries

Scenario: Reconciliation under exchange failure
  Given the exchange returns 5xx and then rate-limit 10018 during reconciliation
  Then the job backs off and retries, reports the run as incomplete, and raises no false divergence alerts

Scenario: Export streams
  Given a 60 000-row export
  Then process memory does not grow proportionally to row count and the asynchronous path is used

Scenario: Budget breach fails loudly
  Given any measured value breaches its declared budget
  Then the CI performance check fails and a defect is filed against the owning ticket
```

## Technical notes / design
Load runs use the E41-Q01 fixtures so perf and functional testing share one dataset definition. Analytics measurements must be taken both cold (cache empty) and warm, and both numbers reported - a warm-only number would flatter the endpoint and hide the real first-open experience that SCR-095's 800 ms budget describes. The E41-K01 benchmark harness is re-run here as a regression check against the tier decision recorded in ADR-0016.

## Test plan
This ticket is the test. Its own gate is that every scenario in Scope has a recorded numeric result or an explicit pass/fail, not a narrative.

## Security notes
Chaos scenario 2 and 5 must confirm that a failure never causes a *silent* data gap - a journal that quietly omits trades is an integrity failure against objective **O8** ("integrity of recorded market data and journal history") in `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`. Load tests run against synthetic data only and use non-production credentials.

N/A (measurement ticket); the scroll benchmark must run with the default density that a11y review approved, not a reduced density that would flatter the number.

## Performance notes
Budgets under test are listed in Context; all results are recorded against them in the R3 PRR evidence pack.

## Observability
Verifies that `journal_analytics_query_seconds`, `journal_materialiser_lag_seconds`, `journal_reconciliation_divergence_total` and `journal_export_duration_seconds` are actually emitted and correctly labelled - an unemitted metric is a defect filed here.

This is the epic's closing gate. `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` requires WCAG 2.2 AA with axe-core in CI **and** manual screen-reader passes; `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 2.2 requires an epic-level regression and exploratory pass plus recorded QA sign-off before E41 can be Done. ## Scope / Deliverables

title: STRIDE threat model and abuse cases for journal & analytics
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` requires a STRIDE threat model per epic and already names the journal's headline concerns: asset **A-12** (trade notes, screenshots, P&L; classification C2/I2/A1), threat **S4** ("journal exports contain account identifiers shared across managers", Medium), control **SR-098** (exports role-scoped, watermarked, audited), objective **O8** (integrity of journal history as evidence), and permission rows 35-37 in section 7.2. This ticket turns those into a worked model with concrete abuse cases before the write and export paths (E41-T04) are reviewed.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **STRIDE model** for the M20 journal trust boundary, documented in `docs/security/threat-models/E41-journal.md`, covering each element: the materialiser's consumption of the execution stream, the Postgres journal tables, the snapshot object store, the analytics query path (including the DuckDB/Parquet path if ADR-0016 selected it), the export job, and the four UI surfaces.
- Per-category analysis with likelihood/impact and a named control, at minimum:
  - **S (Spoofing)**: forging an auto tag so a manual decision appears rule-derived; impersonating the exporting identity in a watermark.
  - **T (Tampering)**: editing a computed field (P&L, R-multiple) to rewrite history; deleting or altering a note to remove evidence; altering the audit trail.
  - **R (Repudiation)**: denying that a note, rating, exclusion or export happened.
  - **I (Information disclosure)**: S4 export scope leakage; IDOR on `journalTradeId`; cross-manager visibility through the account breakdown; snapshots served without authorisation; scope-blind response caching; error messages disclosing the existence of out-of-scope entries.
  - **D (Denial of service)**: an unbounded export or a seven-breakdown query over a huge range exhausting the API; snapshot capture back-pressuring the execution stream.
  - **E (Elevation of privilege)**: a Viewer obtaining write access via PATCH; a Manager widening `account_ids` beyond their grant; a Parquet/DuckDB path bypassing the API's scoping.
- **Abuse cases** written as adversarial narratives with the tester actions that prove the control, handed to E41-Q01 charter (c) and E41-X02:
  1. Manager B enumerates journal trade ids to read Manager A's trades;
  2. a user exports "all accounts" by tampering with the request parameters;
  3. a user edits a losing trade's P&L to improve their record;
  4. a user removes an audit-relevant note after a bad trade;
  5. a user injects script into a note to attack the Owner's session;
  6. a user requests every breakdown over a ten-year range repeatedly to degrade the API;
  7. a departed manager's cached analytics response is served after their grant is revoked.
- **SAST/DAST rules**: a Semgrep rule asserting that every journal repository query carries the account-scope predicate, a rule forbidding raw HTML rendering of note content, and an OWASP ZAP scan profile for the `/journal/*` routes.
- **Permission verification matrix** for rows 35-37 of `04-security-program.md` section 7.2, listing the exact test that proves each cell.
- Findings entered into the risk register where they change a rating.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the controls (E41-T01/T04); the security review of the built code (E41-X02); the R4 pen-test (E43).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Model completeness
  When the model is reviewed by the Security engineer and the Architect
  Then every element of the journal trust boundary has all six STRIDE categories considered, each with either a named control or an explicitly accepted risk signed by the Owner

Scenario: Abuse cases are executable
  Then each of the seven abuse cases states the attacker, the precondition, the exact request or action, the expected defensive behaviour, and the test that proves it

Scenario: Rules land in CI
  Then the Semgrep scope-predicate rule and the note-rendering rule are merged into the CI security job and fail a deliberately introduced violation

Scenario: Cache poisoning by scope covered
  Then the model explicitly addresses analytics response caching keyed without scope and names the test that proves the scope is part of the cache key
```

## Technical notes / design
Two findings deserve special attention because they are easy to miss and cheap to fix now: (1) the deliberate disclosure agreed in E41-D03, where an out-of-scope trade-group leg is shown as "not in your scope" rather than omitted - this is a *reviewed* information-disclosure decision, chosen because silently omitting a leg misstates group P&L; the model must record the reasoning and its bounds (no symbol, size or P&L disclosed, only existence). (2) grant revocation timing: a cached analytics response or an in-flight export must not outlive the grant that authorised it.

## Test plan
The abuse cases are the test plan; they are executed by E41-Q01 charter (c) and verified in E41-X02. The Semgrep rules are tested with deliberately violating fixtures.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security artefact. Data classification A-12; it must itself contain no real account identifiers.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
The DoS analysis sets the hard bounds implemented elsewhere: the export async threshold (50 000 rows), a maximum analytics range, and the bounded snapshot work queue.

## Observability
Specifies the security-relevant events that must be observable: `journal_authz_denied_total`, export audit entries, and an alert on an anomalous export volume.

title: Security review of journal writes, scoping and export controls
body:
## Context
E41-X01 modelled the threats; this ticket verifies the built system against them. It is the security gate for the epic and a prerequisite for the QA sign-off in E41-Q03. The focus is the three places where the journal can actually do harm: **export** (threat S4, control SR-098, risk R13), **scoping** (horizontal escalation between managers), and **integrity of evidence** (objective O8 - computed fields immutable, writes audited, notes versioned).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **White-box review** of `services/api/journal/` against the threat model: every repository query inspected for the account-scope predicate; the PATCH field allowlist; the note sanitiser and its allowlist; the auto-tag provenance and suppression logic; the export scoping, watermarking and audit path; the analytics cache key.
- **Executed abuse cases** 1-7 from E41-X01, each with recorded evidence (request, response, log/audit entry).
- **Authorisation testing** per `04-security-program.md` section 10: horizontal (Manager A -> Manager B), vertical (Manager -> Owner), IDOR on `journalTradeId` and on note ids, across every journal route and both UI and API entry points; grant-revocation timing against cached analytics and in-flight exports.
- **Export verification**: automated assertion that no export in any format contains an API key, key identifier, credential or exchange account secret; watermark present and correct in both CSV and Parquet; audit entry written with the applied filters and scope; the 50 000-row async threshold enforced server-side and not bypassable by a crafted request.
- **Injection testing**: stored XSS via note markdown, tag names and setup/mistake text, verified both at storage and at render; SQL injection attempts on the filter and `group_by` parameters.
- **DAST**: the ZAP profile from E41-X01 run against `/journal/*` with findings triaged.
- **SAST**: CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit results for the journal module reviewed with zero unresolved high findings.
- **Sign-off**: a written security review comment stating pass, pass-with-conditions, or fail, with every finding either fixed or recorded as an accepted risk with Owner sign-off.

## Out of scope
- The external pen-test (E43, R4); rewriting controls (defects are filed against the owning ticket); infrastructure hardening.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: No export leaks scope
  Given a Manager granted exactly one account
  When they export via the UI and again via a directly crafted API request widening account_ids
  Then both exports contain only that account's trades and the widened request is rejected server-side

Scenario: Exports contain no secrets
  When exports are produced in CSV and Parquet across every filter combination under test
  Then an automated scan finds no API key, key identifier, credential or account secret in any output

Scenario: Evidence is tamper-evident
  When an attempt is made to modify realised_pnl or r_multiple via the API
  Then it is rejected with 422, the stored value is unchanged, and the attempt is logged

Scenario: Note history survives deletion attempts
  When a note is edited to remove incriminating content
  Then the prior revision is retained and the edit is audited

Scenario: Stored XSS blocked
  When a note, tag name or setup field containing script payloads is stored and later rendered in the Owner's session
  Then no script executes, at storage or at render

Scenario: Grant revocation
  Given a Manager's account grant is revoked
  When a previously cached analytics response for that scope is requested
  Then it is not served, and any in-flight export for that scope is cancelled or completes containing only still-authorised data

Scenario: Gate
  Given any unresolved high or critical finding
  Then security sign-off is withheld and E41-Q03 cannot complete
```

## Technical notes / design
Review the analytics cache key explicitly: scope-blind caching is the single most likely way this epic's RBAC gets defeated, and it is invisible in a functional test because every individual request looks correct. Likewise verify the ADR-0016 query path - if analytics reads Parquet directly, confirm the scope predicate is applied in that path too rather than only in the Postgres path.

## Test plan
Abuse cases executed manually with evidence; automated assertions (secret-scan on exports, Semgrep scope-predicate rule) wired into CI so the controls cannot silently regress after this review; ZAP scan automated in the security pipeline.

## Security notes
This is the security review. Findings are rated per `04-security-program.md`; high and critical findings block the R3 gate. Evidence is stored in the security evidence pack for the R3 PRR and the R4 pen-test's scoping input.

## Accessibility notes
N/A, except that the export confirmation copy asserting scope, watermark and audit must be verified as *present and accurate* - a control the user cannot perceive is not a control.

## Performance notes
Verifies the DoS bounds from E41-X01: the analytics range cap, the export async threshold, and that the snapshot queue cannot back-pressure the execution stream.

## Observability
Confirms `journal_authz_denied_total` increments on every denial and that export and mutation audit entries are complete, correct and append-only.

- [ ] All seven abuse cases executed with evidence attached.
- [ ] Authorisation, injection, DAST and SAST results triaged; zero unresolved high or critical findings.
